title: Casper and the Tide
premise: Vesper Halloran, a pastry chef drowning in debt and guarded by old heartbreak, hires Casper Reyes—a charming stranger with a lawyer's eye for loopholes—to pose as his boyfriend at a family reunion that doubles as a fight over his late mother's estate. What begins as a transaction turns real, but Casper is hiding that he's investigating the predatory lender squeezing Vesper's café dry, a firm tied to Vesper's own uncle. When the truth surfaces mid-reunion, Vesper must choose between the safe distance he's always kept and the man who broke the rules to save him. Together they expose the scheme outside the courtroom—through ledgers, testimony from other victims, and the found family of the café's regulars—and Veper learns that risking the whole heart is the only payment worth making.
about_author: Gideon Okafor is the pen name of a former line cook turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, courtrooms, and the spaces where justice gets personal. He lives near the coast, where he claims all his best plot twists arrive on the tide.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A final notice arrives the same morning as an invitation to the Halloran family reunion—where his uncle will announce he's buying the building out from under him. Vesper invents a boyfriend on the spot to deflect pity. Emotional beat: pride masking panic; the reader feels how close everything is to collapse.

chapters.title: The Stranger at Table Six
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper, a paralegal quietly gathering evidence against Marrow Lending Group, overhears Vesper's lie and offers himself up as the fake boyfriend—for free, which should be a red flag. Emotional beat: magnetic first meeting; two people each hiding something, both convinced they're the only one lying.

chapters.title: Rehearsing the Truth
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over stolen afternoons in the closed café, they build a fake history—first date, inside jokes, how they met—and Casper keeps steering questions toward Vesper's loan paperwork. Emotional beat: intimacy growing under false pretenses; the rehearsal starts feeling like the real thing.

chapters.title: Saltwater House
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The reunion at the family beach house: Vesper arrives with Casper on his arm and watches his siblings' faces change. Uncle Aldous is charming, watchful, and asks Casper what he does 'exactly.' Emotional beat: dread and belonging tangled together; Vesper realizes he brought armor that looks like a heart.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. By dessert the fake relationship has stopped being performance—Vesper laughs with his whole body, and Casper forgets his cover story twice. Then Aldous mentions Marrow Lending by name, and Casper realizes the family connection runs deeper than he thought. Emotional beat: falling in love and uncovering betrayal in the same breath.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper confirms Aldous funneled desperate borrowers—including Vesper—into Marrow's predatory terms, skimming the difference. He plans to hand the evidence to the state attorney but hesitates, knowing it will detonate Vesper's family. Emotional beat: the cost of doing right; loyalty split down the middle.

chapters.title: Pieces, Not the Whole
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper finds Casper's case files hidden in the café office—the investigation, the photos of their 'dates' annotated like surveillance. Feeling used, he throws him out and signs Aldous's buyout papers in grief. Emotional beat: heartbreak as self-protection; the past tense reasserting itself.

chapters.title: The Regulars
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, mostly Vesper's POV. The café's found family—Ruthie the retired teacher, Dev the night-shift nurse, teenage Theo on dish duty—refuse to let Vesper sign away the place. They reveal other borrowers Marrow ruined and propose fighting publicly, not legally alone. Emotional beat: grief interrupted by community; survival reframed as collective.

chapters.title: Low Tide
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. At the reunion's closing dinner, Vesper stands and reads the ledger aloud—Aldous's skim, Marrow's terms, names of neighbors—while Casper delivers the files to the attorney general's office. Aldous's allies scatter; the buyout dies. Emotional beat: climax; justice outside the law, paid for with exposure and blood-family rupture.

chapters.title: Whole Heart, Rising Tide
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, epilogue-flavored. Months later: the café survives on a community-backed refinancing, the case moves forward, and Casper waits at table six every morning until Vesper finally sits down—not as a client, not as a mark, just as himself. Emotional beat: resolution; lending pieces was never enough, and the whole heart turns out to be survivable.
